stem_book: In a flask, colourless N₂O₄ is in equilibrium with brown coloured NO₂ [N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)]. At equilibrium, when the flask is heated at 100°C the brown colour deepens and on cooling it becomes less coloured. The change in enthalpy ΔH for the system (N₂O₄ → 2NO₂) is: (a) negative (b) positive (c) zero (d) undefined
reason: Added the reaction direction N₂O₄ -> 2NO₂ so the sign of ΔH is defined
work: heating deepens NO₂ colour -> forward favoured by heat -> ΔH > 0
